chapter: Other Philadelphia work and the union
title: Philadelphia's two unions and joining local 802 in New York
summary: Waters joined the Black local in Philadelphia at about 16 and only joined New York's local 802 around 1926, when he came with Charlie Johnson from Atlantic City.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: There were two unions in Philadelphia?
Two unions, yeah.
Right, and they go in -
Yeah -
And you joined -
Two unions here, too.
Right - two unions period, in fact. Right.
Yeah.
But you joined - did you join the black local in Philadelphia at that time?
Yeah, I had to, had to -
At -
to work -
And probably at the age of 16 or so?
Yeah. I had to, to work, yeah.
[ ] of all union jobs.
I didn't go, I didn't join the white local until I came to New York, see. Then as
Benny Waters JOHP 6/6/82
soon as they joined, going uptown, they joined the, this uptown on 133rd Street. The Symphony Club or somethin' like that.
PS: Clef Club.

Clef Club, that's it. Instead, it was on 133rd Street anyway, or somewhere in that neighborhood, 'thirty-first or - anyway, as soon as we go in there, I was asked or persuaded to join 802. So I joined, may number is 130, real low - just 1-3-0-W. That's why I'm honorary members.
When did you join the 802 local?
When I came to New York I had to.
No, I know, but -
About 1926. See, I came to New York from Boston and played the Lafayette Theater in 1924, like I told you yesterday.
But you didn't join the union then.
No, I didn't have to.
Right, [ ].

No, I just worked there for two weeks and went on back to Boston. But when I came to New York, I came here with Charlie Johnson's band directly from Atlantic City. And we all had to join the, these - all those that didn't belong to the local, like Jabbo and so forth, they had to join the local. And that's when I joined, see. It was, I forget the name of the street now, where it used to be there.
